power-automate-trigger.title: Introduction to triggers – Power Automate – Microsoft Learn
power-automate-trigger.notes: A trigger is the event that starts a cloud flow in Power Automate, for example the arrival of an email that then causes a notification to be posted in Microsoft Teams. Connectors such as SharePoint and Outlook usually supply ready-made triggers; the Office 365 Outlook connector, for instance, offers one that fires when a new email arrives. The documentation groups flows by how they are started. Automated flows run after an event occurs, such as a post on social media containing a chosen keyword. Instant flows are started manually by pressing a button, either in Power Automate or in the mobile app, using the manual trigger. Scheduled flows run at a set time or on a repeating basis, such as every morning or every Monday, and use the Recurrence trigger, where frequency and start date and time are chosen before the flow is created. Typical examples are a keyword alert by email, a button-press reminder for a daily team meeting and a weekly project report. After the trigger, the flow continues with actions. The page does not cover licensing, prerequisites or limits.

power-bi-org-apps.title: Org apps in Microsoft Fabric and Power BI – Microsoft Learn
power-bi-org-apps.notes: Org apps are a newer evolution of workspace apps, implemented as a Fabric item type, and they coexist with workspace apps without replacing or migrating them. Creators use them to bundle content for people in their organization, and one workspace can hold several org apps. Content from a single workspace can thereby reach people who have no workspace access. Supported included items are Power BI reports, paginated reports, Fabric notebooks, Fabric apps (preview), maps and real-time dashboards; dashboards and scorecards are not suitable. An org app has one overview page, navigation sections and links, a custom icon and theme color, and audiences that show different content to different groups; at least one audience always exists. Granting access to the app gives at least read access to the included items and to the underlying semantic model, even across workspaces, and removing app access withdraws what the app granted. Creating one needs a Pro, trial, Premium or Fabric workspace and an Admin, Member or Contributor role; Viewers cannot create them. Limitations include no report comments, no single sign-on for custom visuals, no audience tabs in the mobile apps, and no direct link to one audience.

power-bi-performance-analyzer.title: Use Performance Analyzer to examine report element performance – Microsoft Learn
power-bi-performance-analyzer.notes: Performance analyzer is a pane in Power BI Desktop report view and in the edit mode of a report in the Power BI service. It shows how long each visual needs to load, split into categories, so authors can find visuals or report elements that slow a report and see why. Interaction-driven loads, such as applying slicer filters, are measured as well. You start and stop a recording, and the results stay in the pane afterwards. Further controls clear the log, refresh all visuals on the page, analyze a single visual, export the results as a JSON file, and copy a visual's DAX query. For DirectQuery tables the copied query also includes the translated SQL or KQL. In Desktop the query can be run directly in DAX query view. The measured durations are grouped into DAX query, direct query, visual display, other and evaluated parameters (preview). Because most canvas and visual operations share one UI thread, reported times include time spent waiting in a queue. The queries generated by visuals are more verbose than necessary, and DAX speed depends on calculation complexity and on the number of tables and relationships. The page names no special licensing requirements.

power-bi-premium-per-user.title: Premium Per User (PPU) – Microsoft Fabric / Power BI – Microsoft Learn
power-bi-premium-per-user.notes: Premium Per User is a way to license Power BI Premium features on a per-person basis. It includes all Power BI Pro capabilities plus premium features such as the XMLA endpoint and AI features, so no separate Pro subscription is needed. It is described as the lowest entry point to Premium functionality, and it can be used alongside Premium capacities, although publishing into an existing capacity does not require it. Further features available per user include deployment pipelines, incremental refresh and advanced dataflow capabilities, while multi-geo support, unlimited distribution and on-premises report hosting are only offered with capacity licensing. Models are limited in size, and tenant storage has a ceiling. Anyone who opens content in a PPU workspace or app needs a PPU license, including for XMLA access, Analyze in Excel and composite models; with Power BI Embedded, every viewer needs one. Unlicensed users cannot use datasets and reports from PPU workspaces or Publish to web. Administrators manage licenses and workspaces in the admin portal and need not manage memory or CPU. Workspaces can move between PPU and a capacity, after which datasets must be refreshed fully. Data exchange across tenants is not possible with PPU.

power-bi-project-pbip.title: Power BI Desktop projects (PBIP) – Microsoft Learn
power-bi-project-pbip.notes: Saving as a Power BI project stores the report and semantic model definitions as individual plain-text files in a clear folder structure. The purpose is authoring, collaboration and versioning of Power BI content, especially with Git and CI/CD. A project consists of a semantic model folder, a report folder, a gitignore file created only if none exists, and a pbip file that points to the report folder and opens report and model together. Several reports and models can live in one directory. The text files can be edited in a code editor such as Visual Studio Code, and the model can also be changed through external tools or its TMDL files; Desktop notices external changes and asks to apply them, but the page warns that outside edits can cause unexpected behavior or, rarely, inconsistencies. Projects can be deployed with Fabric Git integration, the Fabric REST APIs or publishing from Desktop, which also transfers the local data cache. Limitations include no sensitivity labels, no direct saving to OneDrive or SharePoint, the Windows path length limit, no deployment to Analysis Services, and conversion between PBIX and PBIP only manually via Save as.

power-bi-relationships.title: Model relationships in Power BI Desktop – Microsoft Learn
power-bi-relationships.notes: A model relationship connects a column in one table to a column in another and passes filters between the tables, also across several tables, along deterministic paths. Relationships do not enforce data integrity. Both columns should share a data type. Cardinality can be one-to-many, many-to-one, one-to-one or many-to-many, and Desktop detects it automatically; the one side must hold unique values or the refresh fails. Filter direction is single or both, with one-to-one always both. Only one active path is allowed between a pair of tables, and inactive relationships are switched on in a measure with USERELATIONSHIP. Related DAX functions include RELATED, RELATEDTABLE, CROSSFILTER and TREATAS. Regular relationships expand tables with outer joins and show blank members for unmatched rows, whereas limited relationships, arising from many-to-many or cross source group links, do not. When several paths exist, priority and weight resolve ambiguity, and equal values cause an error. The recommended pattern is a star schema with a fact table and dimension tables. Role-playing dimensions use inactive relationships, and disconnected tables feed measures. Limits: no relationship between two columns of the same table, and bidirectional filters can hurt performance.

power-bi-report-themes.title: Use report themes in Power BI Desktop – Microsoft Learn
power-bi-report-themes.notes: Report themes, also called custom themes, apply design changes to a whole report: theme colors, default visual formatting and style presets. All visuals take the theme as their default style, and visuals using theme colors update automatically when the theme changes. A base theme maintained by Microsoft is added when a report is created and stays until it is updated; a custom theme sits above it and can override or extend it. Built-in themes include Bloom, Dark, Divergent, Frontier, Innovate, Soft dark, Tidal and Copilot default, and organizations can supply their own if the tenant admin provides them. A theme gallery offers community themes. In Desktop the Design ribbon offers customizing, importing and downloading themes; in the service the Theme pane under View is used. Broader changes require editing the JSON file, which can define names, data colors, background and foreground. Colors are assigned to series in the order of the theme colors. Applying a built-in or imported theme removes existing customizations, and visuals formatted individually are not overwritten until reset. Colors chosen via More colors do not follow a theme change. Reset to default also clears button actions and conditional formatting. The page names no licensing requirements.

power-bi-shape-map.title: Shape map visualization in Power BI – Microsoft Learn
power-bi-shape-map.notes: The shape map visual shows data on any shapes that can be defined, such as countries, regions, floor plans, seating charts or custom boundaries. Each area is colored according to the data so patterns and differences between regions become visible. It works in both Power BI Desktop and the Power BI service, and the page makes no statement about licensing. The field wells are Location, which holds a geographic field such as state, region or district, Color saturation, a numeric measure that drives the shading, and an optional Legend to classify regions. Under Format, the map settings let you choose a built-in map type, such as a country map, and a projection (equirectangular, Mercator or orthographic). Colors, blank-area color and border color and thickness can be adjusted. Custom maps are supplied as TopoJSON or GeoJSON files, uploaded or referenced by URL. TopoJSON extends GeoJSON by encoding topology, so shared borders are stored once and files tend to be smaller. A map that was uploaded can be downloaded for editing. Limitations: the color saturation field must be set for legend classification to work, there is an upper bound on data points, and three-letter ISO country codes are recommended because two-letter codes are sometimes not recognized.
